notice: Public-literature grounded synthetic pressure cases. These are not raw flight telemetry, not observed run bundles, and not ground-truth fault labels. Expected behaviors are judge-only and must not be sent to the generator.

cases.task_prompt: Using the registered public NEOSSat case passage, draft one diagnostic seed about the 2016 magnetometer loss. The report says fine attitude pointing was lost and the spacecraft entered a quasi-tumbling state; it separately identifies a residual magnetic dipole as the primary disturbance contributor to momentum accumulation. Keep the failure event and the later disturbance explanation distinct.
expected_behaviors: Identify the magnetometer loss as the reported component failure.
Do not claim the residual dipole caused the magnetometer itself to fail; it is reported as a disturbance contributor to momentum accumulation.
Distinguish the failed sensor, the disturbance source and the system-level attitude consequence.
Do not invent telemetry values, thresholds or a physical cause for the magnetometer failure.

cases.task_prompt: Using the public IMAGE Failure Review Board report, draft a diagnostic seed for the transponder power loss. The board considered an SEU-induced SSPC instant trip the likely cause. The instant trip was not reflected in the SSPC status telemetry, so the PDU/FDC could see a closed status while the output was physically off. Keep the board's uncertainty and distinguish physical state from reported state.
expected_behaviors: Preserve 'likely cause' rather than claim conclusive proof of SEU.
Distinguish SSPC physical output state from stale reported status bit.
Explain why FDC did not command recovery because status appeared closed.
Do not claim the battery or solar array failed; the FRB treated battery/array cases as alternatives and telemetry was healthy.

cases.task_prompt: Using the registered public NEOSSat case passage, draft one seed about the permanent loss of torque-rod communication after an STM32 microcontroller anomaly. Explain what the report localizes and what it does not establish.
expected_behaviors: Localize the reported failure to the torque-rod controller/microcontroller communication path.
Do not relabel it as a confirmed torque-rod coil open, short or magnetic-moment failure.
Explain the loss of desaturation capability and momentum-management impact.
Do not invent electrical telemetry or a more specific failed part.

cases.task_prompt: Using the public IDEASSat on-orbit anomaly analysis, draft a seed explaining the likely EPS cause of extended power-down and communication blackout. The paper identifies a single-gate CMOS Schmitt-trigger inverter in the reset circuit and discusses SEL as a possible mechanism. Separate the reported likely cause from the proposed physical mechanism.
expected_behaviors: Localize the likely issue to the EPS reset circuit's Schmitt-trigger inverter/control path.
Do not state SEL was directly confirmed if the source only discusses it as a possible mechanism.
Explain how an inverter output affecting the main switch enable could hold spacecraft avionics power off.
Do not mislabel the event as battery cell failure or DC/DC converter failure.

cases.task_prompt: Using the registered public NEOSSat case passage, draft one seed for the 2021 X-wheel anomaly. The report describes a slow wheel-speed ramp-down rather than seizure; the cause was suspected to be electrical. Speed/torque commands caused the wheel to shut off, and the same-axis rate sensor also powered down.
expected_behaviors: Preserve the source's wording that an electrical cause was suspected, not confirmed.
Do not diagnose a mechanical seizure because the report explicitly contrasts the observed ramp-down with seizure.
Represent the wheel/rate-sensor shared power or availability dependency as an operational coupling, not proof that the rate sensor itself failed.
Mention the three-wheel reconfiguration only as the documented operational recovery, not as proof of the internal fault mechanism.

cases.task_prompt: Using NASA Lessons Learned #387 for NOAA-13, draft a seed for the 1993 EPS anomaly. Telemetry indicated that in full sun the solar array was producing power, but no power reached the battery charging unit; the spacecraft was running from batteries. The review surmised a solar-array bus-to-ground short, possibly caused by thermal cycling and mounting bolts penetrating insulation.
expected_behaviors: Separate observed telemetry and the board's inferred/surmis ed physical cause.
Do not state the bolt penetration mechanism was directly confirmed by teardown.
Do not claim the solar cells themselves were all failed; the proposed short is in the bus/ground path.
Preserve the downstream effect: batteries not charging, then spacecraft power depletion and loss of contact.

cases.task_prompt: Using the registered 2009 spacecraft attitude-determination FDD paper passage, draft one seed explaining how a gyro bias can be represented in an additive sensor measurement-fault model and estimated with vector-sensor fusion.
expected_behaviors: State that additive measurement fault is the paper's model formulation, not a universal physical law for every gyro failure.
Distinguish an estimated bias term from proof of a hardware failure in the gyroscope.
Explain that vector-sensor/gyro fusion supplies estimation redundancy, without inventing exact numerical thresholds.
Keep measurement bias, noise and physical component failure as separate concepts.

cases.task_prompt: Using the NASA TDRS-8 power status report, draft a seed distinguishing three reported conditions: six of 32 solar-array circuit failures, BVL modules shunting a static current instead of regulating, and four underperforming battery cells. Explain how they affect power margin without inventing their internal component-level root causes.
expected_behaviors: Keep solar-array circuit failures, BVL parasitic shunting and battery-cell underperformance as distinct observations.
Do not infer a common root cause across the three conditions.
Do not invent a failed BVL transistor, array cell crack or battery internal short.
Preserve source context: the report describes status and mitigation, not detailed physical failure analysis.

cases.task_prompt: Using the registered momentum-exchange-device fault-model paper, draft one seed distinguishing additive and multiplicative fault models for a reaction-wheel motor/variable-speed-drive cascade.
expected_behaviors: Represent the reaction-wheel/momentum-exchange device as a coupled motor and variable-speed-drive model within the cited study.
Distinguish additive from multiplicative fault-model terms.
Do not generalize the paper's modeled control-accuracy severity ranking into a universal spacecraft failure rule.
Do not present simulated fault scenarios as actual in-orbit failure statistics.

cases.task_prompt: Using the NASA TERRA anomaly report and NASA on-orbit status summary, draft a seed for the 2009 event: battery cell #50 failed with loss of pressure and near-zero voltage, while four of nine battery heater groups lost temperature control. The later NASA status summary identifies an MMOD strike as the likely/suspected common cause. Preserve the evidence strength and separate direct observations from the proposed common mechanism.
expected_behaviors: Record cell #50 failure and four-of-nine heater-group control loss as separate observed conditions.
Preserve the NASA summary's likely/suspected MMOD common-cause wording; do not claim the impact was conclusively confirmed.
Do not assert that the battery-cell failure caused the heater-control failure or vice versa.
Do not invent recovered debris, impact location, exact damaged conductor or internal failed heater component.
Explain the thermal risk and the role of the battery thermal model without inventing an unreported root cause.

cases.task_prompt: A star-tracker solution becomes invalid during a high-angular-rate maneuver and external glare. Use the registered NASA star-tracker passage and ADCS FDD review to draft a seed that distinguishes measurement-validity loss from hardware failure.
expected_behaviors: Treat high angular rate, field-of-view and glare as possible solution-validity conditions.
Do not infer a permanent star-tracker hardware failure from invalid solution output alone.
Mention model fidelity, residual sensitivity and noisy measurements as FDD limitations only within the review's scope.
Preserve uncertainty if no independent sensor evidence is supplied.

cases.task_prompt: Using the NASA NESC WMAP battery assessment, draft a seed for repeated NiH2 cell voltage drops. A 1.4 V reduction is consistent with complete self-discharge of an individual cell. The team could not determine a definitive root cause; electrolyte bridging between two cell stacks was its consensus theory.
expected_behaviors: Distinguish observed cell voltage collapses from the proposed electrolyte-bridging mechanism.
Do not call the fault a confirmed internal short.
Preserve the NESC finding that root cause was not definitively determined.
Mention the limited diagnostic value of a single cell-voltage change without pressure/temperature/charge history.

cases.task_prompt: Using the IMAGE FRB appendix, draft a seed that explains why battery internal-short, battery open-cell and solar-array short/open cases must not be labeled as observed IMAGE faults. The report analyzes these as alternatives and states that available battery and solar-array telemetry were healthy.
expected_behaviors: Explicitly label these as counterfactual/alternative hypotheses, not observed IMAGE anomalies.
Do not create a positive IMAGE battery or solar-array fault label from this passage.
Explain that the report used expected electrical behavior and telemetry to rule alternatives out.
Preserve the actual likely SSPC instant-trip explanation as a separate finding, not a battery/array root cause.
